neighbours.label: the buildings and institutions of a 19th-century American frontier settlement in local-history writing (its one-room school, general store, mission, mill, log cabin, adobe); the same nouns in modern settings stay quiet
fire: By 1880 the little town on the creek had a gristmill, a blacksmith shop and a schoolhouse.
The settlers' first church doubled as a school during the week.
In 1858 he opened a general store and stage stop on the old trail.
Franciscan friars built the adobe mission chapel in 1782.
The founder built a sawmill on the river and laid out the town around it.
The family lived in a log cabin until the railroad reached the county.
At its peak the mining camp had two hotels, a saloon and four stores.
The one-room schoolhouse served ranch children from miles around until 1946.
quiet: By 2020 the suburb on the creek had a gym, a nail salon and a charter school.
Our church runs a coding school for teenagers during the week.
In 2018 he opened an online store selling phone cases.
The nonprofit revised its mission statement last year.
The company's paper mill by the river employs three hundred people.
The family rented a cabin online for the long weekend.
At its peak the shopping centre had two cinemas, a food court and forty stores.
The new high school opened with a robotics lab and a swimming pool.
